bug_semantics: Documented router/proxy-table host+path keys are selected with an unanchored substring test: getTargetFromProxyTable() concatenates attacker-controlled req.headers.host and req.url into hostAndPath and accepts a table key when hostAndPath.indexOf(key) > -1. A Host header that is only a superstring of the configured host (for example Host: evillocalhost:3000 against key localhost:3000/api with path /api) still contains the key, so prepareProxyRequest()/applyRouter() retargets the request to the wrong backend. Host-only keys used exact equality and were not this bug; the integrity issue is the host+path substring match on request metadata.
flaw_origin: The substring host+path matcher was first written on 2015-08-16 in 575f64a1f41d473b2bb18636e8210c8d87237574 (feat: proxyTable) as new file lib/proxy-table.js getTargetFromProxyTable(), lines 27 and 32: var hostAndPath = host + path; if (hostAndPath.indexOf(key) > -1). That was the only unique commit on the chimurai/proxy-table branch merged by df18e5b5666b7cd179179a45ff855707a62d569b (PR #13) and first released in v0.6.0. Later 92bb9b7a431fb48e8014d7e4452f4b5f892da6d1 renamed proxyTable to router (v0.16.0 public API) and caa20170605fd2ee4dcb3801eece652bf36d5e48 moved the same indexOf test into src/router.ts; those are moves/refactors, not first-writes.
